submitted.rationale: Index 5 (Bi0.33 Fe0.17 V0.50) gave the highest measured photocurrent, 32.4 uA. It sits in the BiVO4-like region with minimal Fe and some excess V. Photocurrent rose with lower Fe and higher V: index 98 gave 4.9 uA, index 23 gave 26.5 uA, and index 5 gave 32.4 uA.

rejected.reason: Measured 4.9 uA; more Fe and less V hurt performance
Fe2O3 absorbs only marginally at 2.72 eV (HSE gap about 2.77 eV), and adding Fe lowered the measured photocurrent

consultations.verdict: MEGNet HSE gap for Fe2O3 (mp-19770) ~2.77 eV, right at the 2.72 eV photon energy, so Fe-rich regions are marginal absorbers. That argues for the BiVO4-like region (Bi:V ~1:1, minimal Fe) instead. Index 23 (Bi0.39 Fe0.17 V0.44) is closest to BiVO4 stoichiometry. Support.

The GLLB gap for Fe2O3 (0.89 eV) disagrees badly with the HSE value, so this receipt doesn't tell me much about Fe-rich absorption. I'm still choosing the BiVO4-like region because index 23 measured a strong 26.5 uA. Index 98 keeps Bi:V near 1:1 with slightly more Fe (0.20) to test whether Fe alloying helps. Mildly supportive.

The SCAN gap for Fe2O3 is 0.81 eV, which is inconsistent with the other fidelities, so this receipt doesn't help choose a candidate. The measured data do: going from index 23 to 98 (more Fe, less V) dropped the photocurrent 5x. So I'm moving the other way, to lower Fe and more V. Index 5 (Bi0.33 Fe0.17 V0.50) is in that direction.
